title: Mike DeLisa, the community nightclub owner
summary: The club closed in 1958 after Mike DeLisa died; he was a landmark who pawned watches, kept the police cooperative and pleased everybody.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, what happened to the club? Business drop off?

Well, what happened to it was, well, it closed in '58. Now, I'm not sure of the date or anything, but about '56, '57, Mike Delisa died. He was a great little guy. I mean, he was -- that was -- I always said that that was a community night club.
What do you mean, community nightclub?
Well, Delisa was a part -- made himself almost a part of the community. And --
Yeah, it was a landmark. And he had savvy. He didn't have too much education, but he was a guy

who wanted to please everybody. And that's how the club got such a wonderful reputation, because people would come there and they felt at ease, and they felt that they could run to him, and then you could go to him and I could go and get paid sometime, and he would have cigar boxes full of watches and rings and all of this. Because they used to do a little gambling downstairs.
A guy would get broke, they'd come up there and pawn their watch and things, and he would give them money. And they'd come back. And it was just that type of thing. Everybody had a word.
And so it made it very, very -- even the police, they were very cooperative. Everything was -- it was just beautiful.
